card.name: Words introducing a clause after doses
card.fires_on: Relative words like "that" (also "they", "is", "counts") placed right after a noun for doses or patients, where a clause describing the dose or patient comes next. Mostly in overdosage and dosing text.

modes.label: that after dose
modes.description: The word "that" follows doses or a dose and starts a clause about their size.
modes.example: Lethality was observed in rats following single oral doses<< that>> were ≥1000 mg/kg

modes.label: that after patients
modes.description: The word "that" follows patients and introduces a description such as their weight.
modes.example: dosing requirements of patients<< that>> weigh more than 100 kg

modes.label: other clause starters
modes.description: A subject word or verb after a dose or patient noun, leading into a description.

card.writes: No clear link to the promoted or suppressed tokens; they look unrelated and mostly noise.
card.plain: It marks the point where a sentence about doses or patients is about to add a describing clause, such as "doses that exceeded...".
